newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa market sees impulses from trade fair.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa market sees impulses from trade fair.

text.p: German cocoa traders said dormant markets for beans and butter should receive a boost from the international, annual confectionery fair ISM, which will run between January 26 and 30 in Cologne.
"Industrial buyers at chocolate plants often hold back with raw materials purchases until after the ISM when they know the size of their orders for 1997," one said.
"Consumers for the time being are shying away from higher mark prices as a result of the firm sterling/mark ratio."
Large confectionery companies were well covered for the first half of the year and others were content with the availability of local stocks for spot purchases, traders said.

They saw futures in a balance -- the impact of anticipated crop supply deficits may be offset by expectations by some that a large physical position held by one trade house may be wound up and exert selling pressure on prices.
Last week's series of weaker than expected European cocoa grind data for 1996 was weighing on sentiment.
Traders saw a lower 1996/97 crop in Ghana and added the harvest in the Ivory Coast now looked likely to be near the long-term average rather than repeating the record result seen in 95/96.
Even with a good crop in Indonesia, this now made a small global deficit possible, perhaps around 50,000-100,000 tonnes, one said.
"But it probably won't be serious enough to justify a rally," he added.
First quarter cif Ivorian bean sellers were little changed from last week at 2.28 marks per kg (2.26), with buyers at 2.20.
The cocoa butter ratio was also unchanged at 2.68, with implied prices ex-works at 6.30 marks per kg versus 6.21 marks last week. Buyers were at 6.15.
